comparison: Both strongly support the finding that fat body is required for disciplined progenitor migration (C2, C3, C18-C21). OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive experimental evidence including imaging, quantitative analysis, and controls. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding with statements about 'compelling evidence' and 'convincing' conclusions. High agreement on this core finding.

Both support the Upd2-JAK/STAT signaling axis (C4, C5, C26), though peer review R2 also includes JAK/STAT necessity claims (C6, C29, C30) that OpenEval separates into R3. OpenEval focuses on establishing the signaling axis through RNAi and reporter data. Peer reviewers describe 'compelling evidence' for Upd2 production in fat body and JAK/STAT activation in tracheal stem cells. Strong agreement on the signaling mechanism.

Partial overlap on receptor expression and ligand-receptor interaction (C27, C28). OpenEval includes these as part of establishing the Upd2-JAK/STAT axis. Peer reviewers accept these observations as supporting evidence without specific comment, encompassed in their overall positive assessment.

Both address JAK/STAT necessity in trachea for directional migration (C6, C29, C30). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple genetic and pharmacological approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'Dome RNAi, Hop RNAi, or STAT92E RNAi expression in tracheal stem cells results in aberrant migration.' Strong agreement on this functional requirement.

Minimal overlap on downstream tissue integrity consequences (C31). OpenEval includes this as part of JAK/STAT necessity findings. Peer reviewers accept this phenotypic consequence without specific challenge as part of overall positive assessment.

Both support JAK/STAT regulation of PCP genes (C7, C8, C32-C34). OpenEval emphasizes ChIP-seq genome-wide evidence and GFP-reporter validation. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'STAT92E likely regulates the transcription of planar cell polarity genes' using ChIP-seq and protein trap lines, describing evidence as 'compelling' and 'convincing.' Strong agreement on transcriptional mechanism.

Both address ChIP-seq technical data (C81-C83). OpenEval emphasizes genome-wide evidence for direct transcriptional regulation. Peer reviewers accept ChIP-seq quality and genomic distribution without question, supporting the transcriptional regulation conclusions. Agreement on technical validity.

Partial overlap on PCP component requirement (C35). OpenEval R5 focuses on functional requirement of PCP components with RNAi and localization data. Peer R3 addresses broader PCP transcriptional regulation. Both support PCP involvement in directional migration.

Both address cellular morphology observations supporting PCP mechanism (C37-C40). OpenEval emphasizes Ft localization and filopodia distribution as mechanistic insight. Peer reviewers accept these cellular details without question as part of overall PCP findings. Agreement on supporting cellular evidence.

Both address vesicular transport of Upd2 (C9, C10, C41-C46), but with different levels of certainty. OpenEval finds strong support from converging pharmacological and genetic evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'some supporting evidence' but express uncertainty about mechanism, asking how Upd2 in vesicles would bind Dome receptor. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer review rates UNCERTAIN - key disagreement on mechanistic clarity.

Both address tissue-specificity control (C47). OpenEval emphasizes this control supports fat body as relevant Upd2 source. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this control as part of overall inter-organ signaling model. Agreement on control validity.

Both address vesicular transport effects on JAK/STAT signaling and migration (C48-C55). OpenEval emphasizes reporter assays showing reduced signaling and specificity controls. Peer reviewers accept this as 'some supporting evidence' for vesicular transport, part of 'compelling evidence' overall, though mechanistic questions remain. Moderate agreement with some uncertainty about downstream mechanism.

Both address Rab specificity control (C56). OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates pathway specificity (Rab5/7 but not Rab2/3). Peer reviewers accept this negative control without question as strengthening vesicular transport findings. Agreement on control validity.

Both address molecular evidence for Upd2-vesicle interactions (C57-C62). OpenEval finds strong support from colocalization, PLA, and co-IP data. Peer reviewers acknowledge this evidence but express uncertainty about how Upd2 in vesicles would bind Dome receptor extracellularly. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer review expresses mechanistic uncertainty - disagreement on mechanistic completeness.

Both address pHluorin reporter assays for vesicle transfer (C63-C65). OpenEval emphasizes functional evidence for vesicle biogenesis and Rab-dependence. Peer reviewers accept vesicle transfer observation but question downstream mechanism of Upd2-Dome binding. Agreement on vesicle transfer observation, uncertainty about subsequent mechanism.

Perfect overlap on transcriptomic evidence (C22-C25). Both support RNA-seq findings showing cytokine activity enrichment and fat body-dependence. OpenEval emphasizes this provides unbiased support for targeted genetic studies. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of 'convincing' evidence without raising concerns. Strong agreement on transcriptional analysis.

OpenEval R10 addresses background knowledge claims (C11-C16) supported by prior citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are established context rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval R11 addresses interpretations and background knowledge (C66-C75). No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these represent contextual claims and interpretations rather than primary experimental findings requiring specific peer assessment.

OpenEval R12 addresses overall study conclusions (C79, C80). No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers' overall assessment that 'evidence supporting the conclusions is convincing' and work provides 'compelling evidence' aligns with OpenEval's support for these synthetic conclusions.
